text: Why can a laser not be built from a simple two-level atom under resonant optical pumping?
choices: Two-level atoms do not exhibit stimulated emission
Because stimulated absorption and emission have equal rates (B₁₂ = B₂₁), pumping can at most equalize the populations, never invert them
Two-level atoms are unable to absorb pump photons
The optical cavity cannot resonate with a two-level transition
explanation: With B₁₂ = B₂₁, the best a resonant pump can do is drive N₂/N₁ → 1, so inversion (N₂ > N₁) is thermodynamically forbidden. Stimulated emission and absorption both occur; the obstacle is the equality of the rates, which three- and four-level schemes circumvent by using distinct pump and laser transitions.
